title: A Escarpment for the Rivergate
premise: Ines Halloran runs salvage and cargo up the Rivergate, a drowned trade route where the salvage fleet buys silence and the river keeps the rest. When a scientific expedition she ferried stops transmitting above the Escarpment, Ines is pulled into a search that forces her to claim the one wreck the fleet has spent years erasing—the ship her father went down with. Racing the fleet by six tides before the monsoon closes the gorge, Ines finds survivors, evidence of the fleet's buried crimes, and a crew that becomes the family she never let herself keep. She surfaces the truth at the river's mouth, trading her invisibility for a home she finally chooses to hold.
about_author: F. M. Brightwater spent a decade working seasonal river freight before turning to writing, and their fiction is known for waterlogged moral landscapes and crews that argue like families. They live in a houseboat they refuse to name, on a river they refuse to leave.

chapters.title: Six Tides to Landfall
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She ferries the Meridian expedition upriver, all business, all exits mapped, and refuses their invitation to stay for the survey. When their radio goes quiet two days later, the fleet offers her a fat contract to forget them. Emotional beat: the ache of being needed and the reflex to refuse it.

chapters.title: What the Sandbar Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines and her skeletal crew—engineer Dov and runaway deckhand Pell—find the expedition's skiff scuttled, deliberately. Fleet patrol boats sweep the reach, asking questions that are really warnings. POV shifts to Pell, who sees Ines decide to lie to the fleet for the first time. Emotional beat: the moment drifting becomes choosing.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They run the gorge narrows at night, past fleet blockades, following a distress beacon the expedition buried as insurance. Ines reveals a sliver of her past: her father's wreck, the Corriander, lies somewhere above the Escarpment, erased from every ledger. Emotional beat: grief disguised as navigation.

chapters.title: Survivors of the Survey
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. They find three expedition members alive in a flooded quarry camp, guarded by a fleet man named Ossler who has gone native out of disgust. The survivors hold data proving the fleet dynamited the Corriander's wreck site to bury evidence of an old massacre. Emotional beat: horror that makes Ines's private grief suddenly public history.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ossler defects with the survivors, and Ines calculates the cost: every port, contact, and safe berth she has is fleet-owned. Dov wants to run for the coast and sell the data quietly; Ines realizes quiet means the truth drowns again. Emotional beat: the price of survival named out loud.

chapters.title: Two Wrecks, One River
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Diving the Corriander's hull, Ines finds her father's sealed log—proof he tried to report the fleet and was left to drown for it. Pell watches Ines surface shaking and understands the captain has been running from this river her whole life. Emotional beat: the past made physical, cold and close.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A fleet strike team, tipped off by a survivor who cracks, traps them at the old weir. Ossler takes a bullet buying the escape, and the Corriander's log is nearly lost to the river. Ines saves it by going into the water herself. Emotional beat: loss that hardens resolve instead of breaking it.

chapters.title: Running the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Tide four of six: the fleet blockades the river mouth and the storm front arrives early. The crew votes—run, hide, or fight—and for the first time Ines lets the vote be real. They rig the Meridian's surviving survey gear to broadcast the evidence fleet-wide as they run the blockade. Emotional beat: a found crew becoming a crew in fact.

chapters.title: The Wreck Comes Up
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax. In the monsoon's first fury, Ines rams the fleet flagship's tow rig, freeing the Corriander's raised hull section as the broadcast goes out on every channel—her father's voice, the fleet's orders, the massacre's names. The flagship founders; the fleet's own crews refuse the order to fire. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as law but as truth too loud to drown.

chapters.title: A Harbor With Her Name On It
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with Pell's coda. Aftermath: the fleet's captains arrested by their own pilots, the river reopened, the Corriander's crew finally recorded. Ines is offered the Escarpment run as her own charter and, for once, accepts. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not fled to—the river no longer a debt but a home.
